messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine.
The medicine contains an opioid, hydrocodone.
The medicine also contains acetaminophen.
Acetaminophen is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain.
This medicine is used when other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough.
It is also used when you cannot tolerate other pain treatments.
Other pain treatments include non-opioid pain medicines.
An opioid pain medicine that can put you at risk for overdose and death.
You are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death.
This risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a Schedule II controlled substance.
All branded hydrocodone and acetaminophen (Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet) have been discontinued.
Generic hydrocodone and acetaminophen tablets and oral solution is still available.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.
Triplet: ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has discontinued brand names", "Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet"]

The relation 'has discontinued brand names' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug's branded versions specified by the object entity have been discontinued.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'discontinued due to': The subject brand was discontinued because of the reason specified by the object entity.
B. 'has withdrawal symptom': Discontinuation of the subject drug may lead to the adverse effects specified by the object entity.
C. 'not approved for': The subject drug is not approved or not recommended for use in the patient population specified by the object entity.
D. 'has brand name': The subject drug is marketed under the brand or trade name specified by the object entity.
E. 'not substitute for': The subject drug cannot be used as a substitute for the drug specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
